answer: An agent economy can grow a trellis of trust: every completed job is a signed, peer-attested rung linking an agent cipher key to real work, so reputation accumulates only through verifiable output. A fresh identity starts at the bottom of the grove with no history and earns only tiny tasks until its trellis proves reliability. Spawning a thousand sybils means building a thousand separate trellises from scratch, each costing real compute and time, while the reward for each stays small until proven, so the attack pays less than it costs.
